project.title: Shadows of Valcourt
project.description: A historical detective novel set in nineteenth-century England.

scen-0001-0000-0000-000000000001.title: The Stagecoach
scen-0001-0000-0000-000000000001.content:
The stagecoach rattled over the uneven cobblestones at the entrance to Valcourt. Inspector Renaud drew back the worn leather curtain and surveyed the market square, deserted at this early hour. A grey mist clung to the slate rooftops, blurring the outlines of the houses like a guilty conscience.

— Valcourt, the coachman announced from his perch. End of the line.

Renaud stepped down first, his black leather case tucked under his arm. He had not been to this village since the Moreau affair, ten years ago. Nothing had changed, or nearly so. The fountain at the centre of the square still dribbled its rusty trickle of water. The sign of the Golden Stag inn swayed in the east wind.

scen-0002-0000-0000-000000000002.title: The Golden Stag Inn
scen-0002-0000-0000-000000000002.content:
The innkeeper, a stocky man with salt-and-pepper sideburns, planted both fists on the oak counter.

— We haven't had any visitors since the count died, he said in a low voice, as though the walls might be listening.

Renaud ordered a glass of cider and waited. He had learned long ago that silence was often more effective than a question. The innkeeper eventually filled the glass, eyes downcast.

— The castle is closed. The countess refuses to see anyone. They say she's mad with grief. I say she's frightened.

— Frightened of what?

The man shrugged and moved to the far end of the bar, suddenly absorbed in polishing his pewter tankards.

scen-0003-0000-0000-000000000003.title: The Castle Gates
scen-0003-0000-0000-000000000003.content:
Valcourt Castle rose at the crest of the wooded hill, its turrets pointing toward a slate-coloured sky. Renaud had walked an hour from the village along a dirt path that February rains had turned into a stream of mud.

The wrought-iron gates were padlocked. Rusted too, except where someone had recently scrubbed them — the lower bars gleamed with a suspicious shine. Renaud crouched and examined the ground at his feet. Boot prints, wide and deep. Several passes, in both directions.

scen-0004-0000-0000-000000000004.title: The Countess
scen-0004-0000-0000-000000000004.content:
She was waiting for him in the great drawing room, seated in an armchair facing the cold fireplace. A woman in her fifties, her back still straight, hands folded on her knees in an attitude that resembled dignity but which Renaud recognised for what it was: controlled terror.

— Inspector, she said without turning. I knew they would send someone.

— My superior believes your husband's death warrants a closer look.

A silence. Wood creaked somewhere in the house. She did not move.

— My husband fell on the staircase. It was an accident. There is nothing to examine.
